### Observed differences

- In the later window, activities A16, A17, A18, and A19 each appear in about 77% of traces, up from about 22% before; activities A20, A21, A22, and A23 each appear in about 23% of traces, down from about 79% before. [OCC001–OCC008]
- The outgoing transition from A15 shifted: before, about 79% of its transitions went to A23 and 22% to A19; after, about 77% go to A19 and 23% to A23. [DIR001]
- Co-occurrence of A15 with A16–A19 rose from about 22% to 77%, while co-occurrence with A20–A23 fell from about 79% to 23%. [REL001–REL008]
- Among the increased set (A16–A19), co-occurrence rose from about 22% to 77%, and with A27 also rose from about 22% to 77% with more interleaving or repetition. [REL009–REL011, REL016–REL018, REL023–REL024, REL029, REL034]
- Among the decreased set (A20–A23), co-occurrence fell from about 79% to 23%, and with A27 fell similarly. [REL035–REL037, REL039–REL044]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which the process switched from executing a block of activities A20–A23 after A15 to executing a block A16–A19 after A15. The direct successor change from A15 to A19 instead of A23, combined with the mirrored participation changes across all involved activities, indicates a routing or branch change. The number of qualifying items (53) is far above the 0.67 expected by chance, and the pattern is consistent across occurrence, direction, and relation indicators. A competing explanation of sampling variation is unlikely given the magnitude and coherence of the differences. The evidence does not specify the exact internal order of the new block, but the relational data show the increased activities co-occur and appear in both orders, suggesting an unordered or parallel execution. [OCC001–OCC008, DIR001, REL001–REL044]
